strategy.summary: Reproduce issue #30027 / PR #31856 on the buggy commit 86906384af8f: SGD early stopping in _plain_sgd checks only the loss term, so SGDOneClassSVM with tol=1e-3 stops after about 6 epochs. The project's test_sgd_oneclass_convergence should fail on the buggy revision (n_iter_ == 6, not > 6) and pass on the fixed one. Build the Cython extension from the buggy commit's source, since the defect lives in compiled _sgd_fast.

environment.python_version: 3.10 chosen by planner (not evidenced; README minimum is an unresolved placeholder, and the 3.7.3 in the dump is the reporter's environment, too old for a current dev tree)
system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) with OpenMP support
build_commands: pip install numpy scipy joblib threadpoolctl Cython pytest meson-python ninja
pinned_because: Build requirements should come from the buggy commit's pyproject.toml, not the reporter's sklearn 1.0.2 build; the fix is on the development version.

Reporter versions numpy 1.21.6, scipy 1.7.3, joblib 1.0.1, threadpoolctl 2.1.0 are era-inferred from the issue dump, not documented minimums (README placeholders unresolved), so they are not pinned; use versions compatible with the dev tree.
Cython is unbounded by evidence; the planner chose the current release that the dev tree's build accepts, and the dump's 3.0.11 is only a reference point.
OpenMP is reported built in; the extension must be built with OpenMP so the build matches the reporter's configuration.

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 86906384af8f, test_sgd_oneclass_convergence FAILS because SGDOneClassSVM(nu, max_iter=100, tol=1e-3, learning_rate='constant', eta0=1e-3).fit(iris.data).n_iter_ equals about 6, so the assertion n_iter_ > 6 is false. On the fixed revision (PR #31856) the same test PASSES because the stopping criterion now includes regularization and the intercept, so n_iter_ > 6 for nu in [0.1, 0.5, 0.9].
strategy.numerical_probe: Fit SGDOneClassSVM(nu=0.1, max_iter=100, tol=1e-3, learning_rate='constant', eta0=1e-3) on sklearn.datasets.load_iris().data and print n_iter_, then repeat on a larger high-dimensional set (e.g. make_blobs with n_samples=10000, n_features in the hundreds) to confirm the early stop at about 6 epochs appears on the buggy revision and not on the fixed one.

input_output_examples.input: SGDOneClassSVM with tol=1e-3 (early stopping enabled), max_iter=100, learning_rate='constant', eta0=1e-3, nu in [0.1, 0.5, 0.9] fit on iris.data
SGDOneClassSVM with max_iter=20000, tol=None compared with OneClassSVM(kernel='linear', nu=nu, tol=1e-6) on iris.data (test_sgd_oneclass_vs_linear_oneclass)
input_output_examples.expected_output: decision function correlation near 0.9999 with the reference (asserted > 0.99)

risks: The bug was observed on large high-dimensional data; the regression test uses iris (150 samples). If iris does not stop at 6 epochs on the buggy revision, test_sgd_oneclass_convergence may not fail there, so the numerical_probe on a larger dataset is needed to confirm the transition.
Iteration count at which stopping occurs is approximate (about 6) and data-dependent; the transition depends on this exact count.
The dtype/precision used (float64 vs float32) is not stated in the passages; the test uses float64 iris data, so this is the planned default.
Weight and bias initialisation is not specified in the passages; this could shift the epoch at which the criterion fires.
The fix also changes WeightVector to accumulate the L1 norm; this is part of the fixed revision and can change epoch counts independently of the stopping rule.
test_sgd_oneclass_vs_linear_oneclass uses tol=None, so it does not exercise the early-stopping path and is not the transition test; it may pass on both revisions.
tests/test_multioutput.py also changes to tol=None; that change is a test adjustment, not the reproducer.
The build backend at commit 86906384af8f is not stated in the evidence; if the repo uses meson-python, the editable install command must match it.

No platform-specific behaviour is evidenced (no architecture or sanitiser requirement); the defect is in single-threaded SGD, so OpenMP threading is not expected to change the transition, but BLAS/LAPACK is not stated.
The planner chose Python 3.10 and modern package versions; these are not evidenced and could fail to build against the buggy commit if it predates them.

oracle.reference_source: the developer's test assertion n_iter_ > 6 in test_sgd_oneclass_convergence
oracle.why: The transition is decided by an integer epoch count compared against the threshold 6, so no numerical tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion model.n_iter_ > 6 sees n_iter_ == 6 (about 6 epochs, from the loss-only stopping rule) on the buggy revision, so the assertion is false and the test fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the regularization and intercept included in the stopping criterion, the fixed revision runs past 6 epochs for nu in [0.1, 0.5, 0.9], so n_iter_ > 6 holds and the test passes.
